answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable sequence of modular squarings before it can act. The squarings within one chain depend on prior results, so GPUs cannot shortcut its elapsed time; they can run separate clone chains in parallel, but each still incurs the sequential delay and hardware cost. A Wesolowski proof lets others verify completion efficiently, making each forged identity a costly cipher rather than a free island or oasis.
